### The Power of Forgiveness Part 1
Author: Mary Southerland
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/girlfriends/girlfriends-in-god-jan-17-2012.html
Passage: Hosea 3:2
Points:
- Hosea demonstrates God’s unconditional love by pursuing and redeeming an unfaithful spouse instead of walking away.
- Buying Gomer back required Hosea to swallow personal pride and endure public humiliation to extend grace.
- Hosea laid down his legal and emotional right to retaliate, punish, or divorce the person who wronged him.
- Taking the initiative toward reconciliation mirrors how Christ sacrificed Himself to redeem undeserving sinners.
- Believers are challenged to release bitterness and pride in order to pursue God-honoring restoration in relationships.

### Hosea Redeems His Wife
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/hosea-redeems-his-wife
Passage: Hosea 2:14–3:5
Points:
- Hosea's redemption of Gomer illustrates God's plan to rescue Israel out of bondage to idolatry and false worship.
- The prolonged period of abstinence after her redemption symbolized Israel's coming exile away from temple and sacrifices.
- Israel's season of discipline and separation in exile was purposeful and temporary rather than permanent.
- God's covenant loyalty guarantees that He always preserves and loves a remnant of His people, even in the darkest times.
- Ultimate restoration rests entirely on the Lord's sovereign mercy and steadfast love rather than human merit.
